title: LearnedFTL: A Learning-Based Page-Level FTL for Reducing Double Reads in Flash-Based SSDs
problem: Page-level FTLs require multiple flash reads to translate logical page numbers to physical page numbers, inducing address translation overhead. This double-read phenomenon significantly increases latency in random access patterns and becomes a critical performance bottleneck.
motivation: Reducing address translation overhead is critical for improving SSD performance and tail latency in storage systems serving latency-sensitive applications.
method: LearnedFTL uses learned indexes (linear models) to replace traditional page-level translation tables. It employs an in-place-update linear model for efficient index construction, a virtual PPN representation to maintain contiguous physical mappings for sorted logical addresses, and a group-based allocation strategy integrated with garbage collection to minimize training overhead.
key_novelty: First application of learned indexes to page-level FTL design that predicts physical page addresses from logical page numbers using machine learning models to eliminate double reads.
contributions: First learned index-based page-level FTL design reducing address translation-induced double reads
In-place-update linear model technique for efficient learned index construction with minimal overhead
Virtual PPN representation enabling contiguous physical page mappings for sorted logical addresses
Group-based allocation and training strategy integrated with garbage collection and rewrite operations

metrics.speedup: 5.5× average P99 tail latency vs TPFTL, 8.2× vs LeaFTL (range: 2.9× to 12.2×)
metrics.other: 55.5% reduction in address translation-induced double reads

primary_theme: Learned-index FTL design for SSD address translation
